code_label: Need for accurate carbon market risk estimation
text_span: Accurately and efﬁciently estimating the carbon market risk is paramount for ensur- ing ﬁnancial stability, promoting environmental sustainability, and facilitating informed decision-making.
rationale: States the paper’s central problem and motivation.

code_label: QCGAN-QAE framework proposed
text_span: A quantum computing-based carbon market risk estimation framework is proposed to address this problem with the quantum conditional generative adversarial network-quantum amplitude estimation (QCGAN-QAE) algorithm.
rationale: Identifies the main proposed framework.

code_label: QCGAN simulates future return distribution
text_span: quantum conditional generative adversarial network (QCGAN) is employed to simulate the future distribution of the generated return rate
rationale: Captures the role assigned to QCGAN in the framework.

code_label: QAE measures the distribution
text_span: whereas quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) is employed to measure the distribution.
rationale: Captures the role assigned to QAE in the framework.

code_label: Generator circuit improved by reordering layers
text_span: the quantum circuit of the QCGAN improved by reordering the data interaction layer and data simulation layer
rationale: Records a specific circuit redesign decision.

code_label: Quantum fully connected layer introduced
text_span: with the introduction of the quantum fully connected layer.
rationale: Records the added circuit component.

code_label: Binary search added to QAE
text_span: The binary search method is incorporated into the QAE to bolster the computational efﬁciency.
rationale: Captures the efficiency-oriented modification to QAE.

code_label: EU ETS simulation improves VaR and CVaR
text_span: The simulation results based on the European Union Emissions Trading System reveals that the proposed framework markedly enhances the efﬁciency and precision of value-at-risk and conditional value-at-risk compared to original methods.
rationale: Summarizes the headline empirical finding.

code_label: Carbon market volatility creates financial risk
text_span: the EU carbon market is fre- quently challenged by price volatility owing to factors such as supply-demand dynamics, policy adaptations, and global eco- nomic condition changes, consequently amplifying the ﬁnancial risks inherent to the carbon market.
rationale: States the market conditions motivating risk estimation.

code_label: VaR and CVaR preferred over volatility and beta
text_span: The focus of both the VaR and CVaR on potential extreme losses renders them indispensable for obtain- ing detailed and accurate risk proﬁles in the carbon market.
rationale: Explains why the paper focuses on these risk metrics.

code_label: Classical methods rely on assumptions and many simulations
text_span: traditional methods for estimating VaR and CVaR, such as Monte Carlo simulations require many simula- tions to achieve a reliable estimate and often operate on implicit assumptions of data probability distributions, which may only occasionally reﬂect reality
rationale: Identifies a limitation of existing classical approaches.

code_label: Quantum methods explored as alternatives
text_span: This has led to the exploration of quantum algorithms as promising alternatives.
rationale: Marks the transition to quantum approaches.

code_label: Most quantum risk studies use pre-assumed distributions
text_span: most studies have simulated distributions using pre-assumed models to generate data, such as the Gaussian conditionally independent model
rationale: Identifies a limitation in prior quantum risk work.

code_label: QCGAN considered promising for real-world distribution simulation
text_span: the quantum conditional genera- tive adversarial network (QCGAN) is regarded as a technology that holds great potential for data distribution simulation in real-world applications such as image generation
rationale: Explains why QCGAN is selected as the generative model.

code_label: First claimed application to carbon market risk
text_span: To the best of our knowledge, this study is among the ﬁrst to apply quantum computing to estimate carbon market risk.
rationale: States novelty claim.

code_label: Quantum generator encodes conditional constraints and noise
text_span: The PQC encodes conditional constraints as an input quantum state |𝜓(y)⟩ and outputs a quantum state |𝜓out⟩ as the generated data sample.
rationale: Describes the generator’s encoding mechanism.

code_label: QAE estimates amplitude as probability
text_span: The goal of the QAE is to estimate the amplitude a and the square of the amplitude a is equivalent to the probability
rationale: Defines the core measurement principle used later.

code_label: VaR and CVaR definitions
text_span: VaR estimates the maximum potential loss of an investment portfolio
rationale: Provides the risk metric definition used in the study.

code_label: CVaR captures extreme losses
text_span: The CVaR calculates the expected value of the loss because it already exceeds the VaR, which makes it better to consider extreme losses
rationale: Defines the tail-risk metric used in the study.

code_label: Loss rate used instead of price
text_span: The loss rate is chosen to measure risk rather than price because, starting from the deﬁnitions of VaR and CVaR, investors tend to pay more attention to the rate of change in price than to its absolute value.
rationale: Explains a key preprocessing choice.

code_label: Historical loss rates used as conditional data
text_span: The historical loss rate for the past N days [yt−N, … , yt−1] is used as conditional data to simulate future data generation for the object.
rationale: Specifies the conditioning input for the model.

code_label: Binary encoding of normalized loss rates
text_span: Binary encoding techniques are used to convert classical data into quantum data.
rationale: Captures the encoding strategy.

code_label: QCGAN generates future loss-rate distributions
text_span: we deployed the QCGAN to simulate the poten- tial future loss rate distributions.
rationale: States the generative task of the QCGAN.

code_label: Discriminator distinguishes real and generated samples
text_span: The most important function of the discriminator is to differentiate between the samples created by the generator and the actual data samples
rationale: Describes the discriminator’s role.

code_label: Binary search narrows VaR target state
text_span: The process starts with a binary search that divides the quantum state into two subspaces based on the median value of all quantum states
rationale: Captures the search strategy for locating VaR.

code_label: VaR decoded from target quantum state
text_span: Finally, obtain the entire target quantum state, which is the quantum state corresponding to VaR.
rationale: States how VaR is obtained from the quantum state.

code_label: CVaR computed from states above VaR
text_span: all quantum states that are greater than the target quantum state correspond to extreme loss rates greater than the VaR.
rationale: Describes the state set used for CVaR.

code_label: Discrete summation used for CVaR
text_span: the CVaR computation transitions from the con- ventional integral to a discrete summation
rationale: Captures the computational form of CVaR.

code_label: Entanglement before rotation improves expressiveness
text_span: placing the entanglement stage before the rotation stage signiﬁcantly enhanced the efﬁciency and expressive capabilities of the quantum circuit.
rationale: States the claimed benefit of the circuit reordering.

code_label: QFC enables full qubit interaction
text_span: The QFC layer comprises a series of CNOT gates and rotation gates to achieve full connectivity among qubits
rationale: Describes the added fully connected layer.

code_label: Weakly fully connected topology may reduce learning ability
text_span: only a one-direction connection exists between all qubits, but this con- nection is not sufﬁcient and may reduce the learning ability
rationale: Identifies a weakness in prior topology choices.

code_label: Binary search reduces VaR time complexity
text_span: The time complexity is logarithmic, speciﬁcally O(log N), where N = 2n is the total number of possible states.
locator: 3.3 Quantum amplitude estimation combined with binary search for measuring risk distribution
rationale: States the efficiency claim for the search method.

code_label: Encoding continuity is crucial
text_span: addressing the problem of encoding continuity is crucial.
locator: 3.3 Quantum amplitude estimation combined with binary search for measuring risk distribution
rationale: Highlights an important methodological concern.

code_label: Discontinuous encoding harms VaR and CVaR accuracy
text_span: The discontinuity of encoding indicates the discontinuity and inaccuracy of the estimated CDF, which in turn leads to the inaccuracy of the estimated VaR and CVaR.
locator: 3.3 Quantum amplitude estimation combined with binary search for measuring risk distribution
rationale: States a caveat about encoding design.

code_label: EU ETS ECX data used
text_span: Our analysis focuses on ECX price data, providing insights into the market’s volatility and trend behaviours
rationale: Identifies the empirical dataset.

code_label: Training-test split without shuffling
text_span: the dataset employed in this study includes carbon market prices from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2020.
rationale: Captures the time span and time-series setup.

code_label: Backtesting used for evaluation
text_span: The evaluation criterion for VaR/CVaR was back testing.
rationale: States the evaluation approach.

code_label: Kupiec test used for VaR backtest
text_span: The backtesting of VaR in this study was performed using the Kupiec test.
rationale: Specifies the VaR validation test.

code_label: DLC used for CVaR backtest
text_span: The backtest of CVaR is the difference between the losses and CVaR (DLC) tests.
rationale: Specifies the CVaR validation test.

code_label: Quantum time cost modeled from circuit depth
text_span: The uniﬁed computation time, considering a single execution of these two processes, is calculated as follows
rationale: Captures the time-cost modeling approach.

code_label: Minibatch discrimination and adaptive GAN used to stabilize training
text_span: we adopted a Minibatch Discrimination technique along with the adaptive GAN approach
locator: 4.1.5 Convergence criteria in CGAN and QCGAN models
rationale: Records the stabilization strategy.

code_label: Ten distinct models trained to address mode collapse
text_span: This was implemented to simultaneously train ten distinct CGANs or QCGANs, effectively addressing the mode-collapse challenge
locator: 4.1.5 Convergence criteria in CGAN and QCGAN models
rationale: Identifies a training challenge and mitigation.

code_label: Original QCGAN fails Kupiec test
text_span: the LR value of the original QCGAN is too large and exceeded the critical value; therefore, it failed to pass the Kupiec test at all three conﬁdence levels.
rationale: Reports a negative performance finding.

code_label: QCGAN-QAE generally best overall
text_span: Overall, a comparison between the historical simulation, CGAN, QCGAN, and QCGAN-QAE shows that the proposed model generally has the best overall effect
rationale: Summarizes comparative performance.

code_label: QCGAN-QAE still limited at 99 percent confidence
text_span: there are certain limitations in its ability to face extreme market risks.
rationale: States a caveat about extreme-risk performance.

code_label: Quantum speedup in runtime
text_span: the required running time is only 1/84,500 (a reduction of 99.9988%) and 1/84,000 of CGAN
locator: 4.3 Computational efﬁciency comparison of optimal result
rationale: Reports the efficiency gain.

code_label: QCGAN-QAE converges in fewer epochs
text_span: QCGAN-QAE requires only 30 epochs to achieve convergence, and the required epochs are reduced by 90% compared to the 300 epochs required by the CGAN
locator: 4.3 Computational efﬁciency comparison of optimal result
rationale: Reports convergence improvement.

code_label: Circuit structure changes improve accuracy
text_span: the estimation accuracy of the modiﬁed QCGAN is signiﬁcantly higher than that of the original QCGAN.
locator: 4.4 Accuracy comparison of QCGANs with different quantum circuit structures
rationale: Summarizes the effect of circuit redesign.

code_label: QFC improves VaR and CVaR at lower confidence levels
text_span: At 90% and 95% conﬁdence levels, those with QFC performed better on both VaR and CVaR.
locator: 4.4 Accuracy comparison of QCGANs with different quantum circuit structures
rationale: Reports the benefit of adding QFC.

code_label: QAE improves accuracy over direct measurement
text_span: The results show that after adding the QAE, the estimation accuracy improves.
rationale: States the effect of QAE on estimation accuracy.

code_label: Binary search accelerates QAE
text_span: Integrating a binary search with the QAE signiﬁcantly improved the time efﬁciency of the model.
rationale: Captures the efficiency gain from combining methods.

code_label: Binary search helps most at lower confidence levels
text_span: when the conﬁdence level is low, acceleration combined with the binary search method is more obvious.
rationale: Notes a conditional performance pattern.

code_label: Higher confidence may reduce binary-search benefit
text_span: When the conﬁdence level is particularly high, the QAE may only be as good as the binary search method.
rationale: States a caveat about the method’s benefit at high confidence.

code_label: Depth sensitivity is limited in tested range
text_span: the performance of the model is not sensitive to the depth choice.
rationale: Reports robustness to depth variation.

code_label: Increasing depth raises overfitting and noise risk
text_span: although increasing the depth of a quantum circuit can lead to more expressive mod- els, it also increases the risk of overﬁtting and the impact of noise.
rationale: Identifies a tradeoff and limitation of deeper circuits.

code_label: QCGAN-QAE advances carbon risk estimation
text_span: this novel quantum computing-based framework signiﬁcantly advances carbon market risk estimation.
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s overall contribution.

code_label: Future work on angular rotation encoding
text_span: we plan on exploring the use of angular rotation encoding, which promises to signiﬁcantly reﬁne the approach to quantum data encoding.
rationale: States a specific future research direction.

code_label: Future work on parameter tuning
text_span: there will an emphasis on ﬁne-tuning the algorithm parameters of the QCGAN-QAE framework.
rationale: States another future research direction.
